narrative.hook: A welder in Tulsa earns $45,800. But a family of four needs $79,924 to cover basics. Where does that leave working families?

sections.title: The Blue Collar Reality
sections.content: Blue collar work built America. But in 2026, can it still support an American family?

sections.title: Tulsa's Edge
sections.content: Housing costs 22.7% less than the national average. That's $4,114/year — real money for working families.

sections.title: The Math Problem
sections.content: Single-income blue collar families face a $35,000+ gap between earnings and living wage. The math only works with dual incomes.

sections.title: Why Tulsa Works
sections.content: Two blue collar incomes in Tulsa = $88K combined. Living wage for 2-working-adult household = $105K. The gap shrinks to manageable.

narrative.callToAction: Tulsa isn't perfect. But for working families, it's one of the better hands you can be dealt.
